key_insight: Deep QSCI combines divide-and-conquer and QSCI to approximate benzene dimer π–π interaction energies with far fewer qubits by reusing a monomer-based reduced basis.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the quantum hardware footprint from a 40-qubit dimer calculation to a 20-qubit monomer calculation, making interaction-energy scans more practical on near-term devices.
method: Run QSCI on one benzene monomer to obtain a ground state.
Generate a reduced local basis using particle-number-conserving one-electron excitations.
Build and diagonalize an effective dimer Hamiltonian from the reduced basis and intermonomer interactions, reusing monomer results across distances.
evidence_signal: In 6-31G**, the method predicts an attractive minimum of -0.91 kcal/mol at 4.0 Å, reasonably close to the counterpoise-corrected CCSD(T) reference of -1.14 kcal/mol.
watch_item: Accuracy may be limited by inconsistent active orbitals/reduced bases between monomers, basis-set dependence, and unresolved charge-transfer effects.
paper_title: A Divide-and-Conquer Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction for Evaluating $π$-$π$ Stacking Interaction Energies in the Benzene Dimer
